title: Antiferroelectric-knee capacitor biased onto ZrO2's steep switching branch
idea: Box = {medium: field-induced polarization in antiferroelectric ZrO2 | access: vertical-channel Si FET | sense: standard charge-share SA | integration: 1T1C with a short pillar | substrate: 300 mm Si | fab: ALD ZrO2/Al2O3 nanolaminate}. The cell plate is DC-biased just below the AFE-to-FE critical field so the +/-0.5 V node swing rides the steep double-hysteresis branch, where dQ/dV equals an effective k of ~100-150; the cell runs minor loops and never reaches full remanent switching, which limits fatigue.
why: Fact 1 capacitor charge wall: 3-5x charge per area lets pillar AR fall from ~70:1 to ~20:1, removing the hardest etch and allowing a tighter pitch.

title: Hole-confining SiGe quantum-well body for capacitorless 3D tiers
idea: Box = {medium: holes trapped in a compressively strained Si0.6Ge0.4 quantum well | access: lateral gate-all-around Si nanosheet | sense: threshold-shift read current (1T0C) | integration: 30-60 tier epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice | substrate: Si | fab: one epitaxy run + staircase etch}. The ~0.35 eV valence-band offset forms a pocket under each nanosheet that holds holes written by impact ionization or GIDL, aiming for 100-1000x the retention of a homogeneous-Si floating body with no capacitor at all.
why: Fact 2: removes the capacitor that blocks 3D DRAM, so tier count rather than lithography sets density; target 4-8x bits/mm2 at 32+ tiers, built mostly with deposition and etch.

title: Conducting charged domain wall in thin-film lithium niobate as bit
idea: Box = {medium: presence or absence of a conducting head-to-head domain wall in LiNbO3-on-insulator | access: Si FET in the CMOS below | sense: nondestructive wall current (on/off ~1e4) | integration: hybrid-bonded LNOI film over logic | substrate: LNOI | fab: ion slicing + e-beam-defined electrode pairs}. A ~3 V pulse between two in-plane electrodes 30 nm apart nucleates or erases a charged wall bridging them; a read only measures conduction through the wall, so polarization never reverses on read.
why: Fact 8 destructive read and Fact 3 refresh: a nonvolatile cell with nondestructive read (NDRO) avoids restore energy (~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and refresh; wall motion needs no oxygen-vacancy drift, so endurance may exceed hafnia.

title: Snap-through buckled nanobeam: contactless mechanical bistable bit
idea: Box = {medium: up or down buckled shape of a pre-compressed 120 nm SiN/Si nanobeam | access: row/column electrostatic electrodes, no transistor | sense: capacitive gap readout through a shared column amplifier | integration: sealed vacuum-cavity array in BEOL | substrate: Si | fab: sacrificial-oxide release + ALD seal}. Built-in compressive stress pushes the beam past Euler buckling so it has two stable shapes; a 1-2 V pulse snaps it through in ~1 ns (GHz resonance), and it never touches a surface, so there is no stiction or contact wear.
why: Facts 3 and 10: zero leakage and zero refresh, elastic switching energy ~1 fJ, endurance limited only by elastic fatigue; removes the access-transistor leakage tail entirely.

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings replace per-bit transistors and capacitors
idea: Box = {medium: charge packets in buried-channel potential wells | access: three-phase clocked ring gates, no per-bit FET | sense: floating-diffusion source follower at the string end | integration: vertical 32-bit CCD strings in deep holes | substrate: Si | fab: 3D-NAND-style hole etch + conformal gate stack}. Each vertical hole is a 32-stage CCD; a random access shifts the string past one amplifier in <30 ns, and every access recirculates and re-amplifies the packets, so refresh happens as a side effect of normal shifting.
why: Facts 2, 4, 7: ~2F2 per bit with no capacitor and no access transistor; density scales with string length rather than lithography, and one amplifier per 32 bits shrinks the periphery.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn tunnel junction with zero stray field
idea: Box = {medium: magnetic octupole order in Mn3Sn | access: Si FinFET | sense: antiferromagnetic tunnel magnetoresistance | integration: BEOL above periphery | substrate: Si | fab: sputtered Mn3Sn on a Pt spin-orbit-torque line, 400 C anneal}. Spin-orbit torque rotates the octupole; with no net magnetization, cells at 15 nm pitch do not disturb neighbors and switch in tens of picoseconds.
why: Density and energy: removes the stray-field pitch limit of ferromagnetic MRAM, sub-100 ps writes at ~10 fJ, built from abundant Mn and Sn.

title: Volatile flash: ultrathin-tunnel charge-trap cells built on 3D-NAND lines
idea: Box = {medium: electrons in a SiN trap layer behind a 1.2 nm direct-tunneling oxide | access: the storage FET itself, NOR-wired | sense: nondestructive threshold read | integration: 200-layer vertical string rewired as NOR | substrate: Si | fab: unchanged 3D-NAND tool set}. Thinning the tunnel oxide trades 10-year retention for ~1-10 s and lets 4-5 V direct-tunneling writes finish in ~10 ns without the Fowler-Nordheim stress that wears out flash, with refresh every second instead of every 64 ms.
why: Facts 2, 3, 4: turns idle, depreciated 3D-NAND capacity into 3D DRAM-class memory with 15x less refresh and 200+ layer density.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN gating a MoS2 channel
idea: Box = {medium: interlayer-sliding polarization of parallel-stacked bilayer hBN | access: MoS2 channel underneath acting as a FeFET | sense: nondestructive channel conductance | integration: BEOL 2D stack on logic | substrate: Si | fab: wafer-scale CVD + transfer}. Polarization flips by an interlayer slip of a fraction of a lattice constant, with no bond breaking or oxygen-vacancy motion, which early reports suggest gives fatigue-free switching past 1e11 cycles at sub-volt fields.
why: Endurance and the voltage floor (Fact 10): sub-volt switching with no ion motion, nonvolatile so no refresh, and an atomically thin storage layer for many-tier stacking.

title: Low-barrier VCMA nanomagnet: deliberately volatile, refreshed-every-second MRAM
idea: Box = {medium: perpendicular CoFeB nanomagnet with a thermal barrier of only ~25 kT | access: vertical Si diode | sense: TMR | integration: BEOL crosspoint at 12 nm | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + ion-beam etch}. Writes use sub-ns voltage-controlled-anisotropy precessional pulses with almost no current, so the MgO barrier is never stressed; the low barrier makes the cell tiny and cheap to write, and a 1 s refresh replaces 10-year retention.
why: Energy (Fact 10) and endurance: ~10 fJ writes, effectively unlimited endurance because no breakdown current flows, and 15x less refresh than DRAM.

title: Hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2 as resistive bit
idea: Box = {medium: metastable hidden CDW domain state in 1T-TaS2 | access: Si FET | sense: ~10x resistance ratio | integration: BEOL film | substrate: Si | fab: MBE or CVD TaS2 + hBN encapsulation}. A ps-to-ns current pulse quenches the electron lattice into the hidden metallic CDW state, and a longer, weaker pulse restores the insulating commensurate state; switching is electronic ordering, not atom migration, so energy is fJ-scale.
why: Energy and endurance via purely electronic order switching: fJ writes and no refresh, but the hidden state has only been shown stable at low temperature.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade dot storing five electrons per bit
idea: Box = {medium: 1-10 electrons on a ~2 nm Si dot | access: tunnel barrier to a 5 nm Si nanowire channel | sense: dot charge gates the nanowire (gain read) | integration: stacked vertical nanowires | substrate: Si | fab: self-limiting thermal oxidation sculpts the dot}. The dot's ~0.3-0.5 eV charging energy blocks back-tunneling, so a few electrons hold state for seconds, and the nanowire current amplifies them for sensing.
why: Energy per bit drops to the aJ scale (Fact 10) with no capacitor (Fact 1): ~1000x less stored charge than a 5 fF cell.

title: Bistable DX-center defect ensemble as charge store in AlGaN HEMT
idea: Box = {medium: electrons captured by DX centers (large lattice relaxation) in Si-doped high-Al AlGaN | access: the HEMT gate itself | sense: 2DEG density shift read as drain current | integration: GaN-on-Si memory tiles | substrate: GaN-on-Si | fab: MOCVD}. DX centers capture hot electrons in nanoseconds, but their lattice relaxation raises a ~0.6-1 eV emission barrier, so trapped charge stays for seconds to minutes; the defect's own physics acts as the capacitor.
why: Facts 1 and 3: a capacitorless store with engineered retention and 100x+ longer refresh intervals, using a defect normally treated as a nuisance.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access device with air-gap zero leakage
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a MIM capacitor | access: 4-terminal NEMS relay with a 5 nm air gap | sense: charge-share SA | integration: relay array in BEOL over the capacitors | substrate: Si | fab: sacrificial release + Pt-coated contacts}. When the relay is open, the only leakage path is the capacitor dielectric, so retention moves from 64 ms to hours and the capacitor can shrink to ~1 fF.
why: Fact 3 leakage tail and Fact 1: removes subthreshold and GIDL tails, eliminates refresh power and bandwidth (16-33% of idle power), and allows 5x smaller capacitors.

title: Core-shell nanocrystal barrier-layer film giving colossal-k planar capacitor
idea: Box = {medium: interfacial (Maxwell-Wagner) polarization in a film of 5 nm conducting doped-TiO2 cores with 1 nm Al2O3 shells | access: Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: planar or very-low-AR capacitor | substrate: Si | fab: colloidal dip coat + ALD shell infill}. Each conducting core acts as a floating plate, so the film behaves like hundreds of series-parallel nanocapacitors with effective k of 300-1000, provided core conductance keeps the relaxation frequency above ~100 MHz.
why: Fact 1: an effective k far above the k~70 target lets the pillar flatten to AR <10:1 and removes the deepest etch steps.

title: Magnetoelectric Cr2O3 antiferromagnet written by voltage, read by Hall
idea: Box = {medium: Neel vector of boron-doped Cr2O3 | access: Si FET | sense: anomalous Hall voltage in an adjacent Pt film | integration: BEOL | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + boron doping to lift the Neel point above 400 K}. Because Cr2O3 is magnetoelectric, its Neel vector flips under a small voltage combined with a static bias field built into the stack, with no charge current through the bit.
why: Energy (Fact 10): aJ-to-fJ write energy, nonvolatile, no current-induced wear, and antiferromagnetic order immune to neighbor disturb.

title: Sequential smart-cut stacking of single-crystal planar 1T1C tiers
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a planar trench-free MIM | access: lateral single-crystal Si FET in each transferred film | sense: SA on the base die | integration: 16-32 tiers by repeated hydrogen-implant layer transfer below 400 C | substrate: reusable donor wafers | fab: low-temperature bonding + splitting}. Each tier is a thin crystalline Si film with near-bulk access transistors, avoiding the poor poly or oxide channels that hurt monolithic 3D.
why: Fact 2: single-crystal channels in every tier remove the lateral-transistor blocker, and reused donor wafers keep substrate cost per tier small.

title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid in nanopores: a ferroelectric that cannot fatigue
idea: Box = {medium: polar ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734-class, P~6 uC/cm2) | access: Si FET | sense: polarization charge released on read | integration: 10-20 nm pores in a BEOL oxide sealed with ALD | substrate: Si | fab: vacuum capillary fill}. At 1 V across 10 nm the director rotates in ~20 ns (tau ~ viscosity/(P*E)), and because the medium is a fluid, defects and domain pinning anneal out instead of accumulating as fatigue.
why: Endurance: a self-healing liquid ferroelectric, unlike hafnia; gives a FeRAM-like cell with large switched charge in a shallow pore instead of a high-AR capacitor.

title: Proton-transfer organic ferroelectric (croconic acid) as low-voltage polar bit
idea: Box = {medium: polarization from collective proton hopping along hydrogen bonds in croconic acid | access: Si FET | sense: FeFET threshold shift | integration: vapor-deposited BEOL layer | substrate: Si | fab: low-temperature thermal evaporation}. Switching moves only protons by ~1 angstrom inside hydrogen bonds, with no heavy-ion motion, which gives coercive fields far below hafnia and lets the layer be deposited below 150 C over finished logic.
why: Voltage floor (Fact 10) and BEOL stacking: sub-1 V nonvolatile switching, and the tiny thermal budget lets many tiers stack.

title: Alignment-free hybrid bonding onto a statistical nanocapacitor carpet
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a carpet of isolated 8 nm DSA-defined nanopillar capacitors | access: transistor wafer with 40 nm landing pads | sense: standard SA | integration: wafer-to-wafer bond with no cell-level alignment | substrate: separate capacitor wafer | fab: block-copolymer DSA + ALD, high-temperature anneal before bonding}. Each pad lands on ~10 random nanocapacitors in parallel, and because each capacitor is smaller than the gap between pads, none bridges two cells; the capacitor wafer can take thermal budgets the transistors could never survive.
why: Facts 1 and 4: separates the capacitor and transistor processes, removes the cell-level overlay requirement and needs no EUV on the capacitor wafer.

title: Imprint-engineered HZO capacitor read nondestructively by small-signal capacitance
idea: Box = {medium: polarization in a deliberately imprinted HZO capacitor | access: Si FET | sense: ~100 mV small-signal capacitance read (butterfly asymmetry) | integration: 1T1C over periphery | substrate: Si | fab: asymmetric TiN/conductive-oxide electrodes set a built-in imprint}. The imprint shifts the C-V butterfly so the two polarization states differ by ~30% in capacitance at 0 V, and the read senses that difference without switching, so reads never wear the ferroelectric.
why: Fact 8 and endurance: no destructive read or restore; the ferroelectric cycles only on writes, so a write-buffering cache makes endurance a non-issue.

title: Morphological-box test chip: 10,000 storage-element combinations per wafer
idea: Box = {all six axes varied on purpose}: a standard periphery wafer carries 10,000 1-kbit tiles, and gradient sputtering, area-selective ALD and maskless e-beam give each tile its own medium, electrode, access device and anneal. On-chip BIST logs retention tails, endurance and disturb automatically, so the morphological box becomes a physical experiment that outputs a ranked Pareto map of combinations every month.
why: Cuts the learning cycle for new storage elements by ~100x and finds non-obvious medium/electrode pairs that single-material programs miss.

title: Ferroelastic remanent-strain bit read by piezoresistive silicon nanowire
idea: Box = {medium: one of two remanent strain states from non-180-degree ferroelastic switching in a relaxor-PT film | access: Si FET | sense: piezoresistive Si nanowire under the film (gauge factor ~100+) | integration: BEOL with the nanowire channel below | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + rapid thermal anneal}. The bit is stored as lattice strain, not charge, and the nanowire's resistance differs by several percent between the two states; the read does not disturb the domains.
why: Facts 3 and 8: nonvolatile, nondestructive read, no restore, and no stored charge that can leak through a junction.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch revived as refresh-free one-transistor SRAM
idea: Box = {medium: bistable node voltage between two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (negative differential resistance) | access: one Si FET | sense: standard bitline | integration: diodes stacked vertically on the drain | substrate: Si | fab: low-temperature epitaxy of delta-doped tunnel junctions}. The two NDR curves cross at two stable points held by valley current alone, so the cell is static like SRAM in a ~8F2 DRAM-like footprint.
why: Fact 3: no refresh and no capacitor, 3-4x denser than 6T SRAM; standby power is set by valley current, which must reach <1 pA per cell.

title: Anodized-aluminum pore template capacitors with domestic hafnium and molybdenum
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD HfZrO in self-organized anodic alumina pores | access: vertical Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C | substrate: U.S.-grown 300 mm Si (Texas) | fab: anodization (no lithography) + U.S.-built ALD tools}. Pores self-order at a pitch set by voltage (~40 nm at ~16 V) and are registered to the transistors by pre-indent dots from a U.S. multibeam e-beam writer; Hf and Zr come from Oregon zircon processing and Mo electrodes from Colorado.
why: Capital/EUV (Fact 4) and U.S. manufacturability: replaces EUV plus high-AR plasma etch for the capacitor layer with a wet electrochemical step at a fraction of the tool cost, and uses no tungsten.

title: Catalyst-etched 200:1 silicon capacitor holes using DSA mesh and Florida HF
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD dielectric in metal-assisted-chemically-etched Si holes | access: buried vertical FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C in bulk Si | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: U.S.-made block-copolymer DSA defines a Au/Ag catalyst mesh, then HF/H2O2 etches straight 200:1 holes}. The HF comes from fluorosilicic acid recovered at Florida phosphate plants instead of imported fluorspar, and the etch needs only wet benches, not imported high-AR plasma etchers.
why: Fact 1: AR beyond the 115:1 target without plasma-etch limits gives Cs ~10 fF or a tighter pitch, with low capital and fully domestic chemistry.

title: MoO2-templated rutile TiO2 capacitor: k of 90 without ruthenium
idea: Box = {medium: charge in rutile-phase TiO2 (k~80-100) | access: Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C pillar at AR ~30:1 | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: ALD from TiCl4 made in the U.S. from Florida/Georgia ilmenite, on a rutile-structured MoO2 bottom electrode from Colorado molybdenum}. MoO2 shares the rutile lattice, so it templates rutile TiO2 at low temperature the way RuO2 does, and light Al doping holds leakage down.
why: Fact 1 calls for k~70: this delivers it with domestic elements, removes Ru (South Africa) from the stack and cuts AR ~2x.

title: SiC deep-depletion inversion-charge cell with hour-long retention
idea: Box = {medium: minority-carrier inversion charge under a SiC MOS gate | access: lateral SiC transfer gate | sense: charge transfer to a floating diffusion + source follower | integration: dedicated SiC memory die bonded to Si logic | substrate: U.S.-made 200 mm 4H-SiC (North Carolina/New York) | fab: U.S. SiC power-device lines}. SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap cuts thermal generation by ~1e-18 relative to silicon, so a deep-depletion well holds charge for hours at 85 C; it is the original inversion-layer 1T DRAM concept, minus refresh.
why: Fact 3: refresh disappears (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth), using U.S. SiC capacity that swings with power-device demand.

title: Aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric FeFET built from U.S. borax and aluminum
idea: Box = {medium: wurtzite AlBN polarization | access: Si FET whose gate dielectric is the AlBN film | sense: nondestructive threshold shift | integration: BEOL plus an SRAM write-coalescing buffer that keeps each cell below 1e9 cycles in 10 years | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: reactive sputtering with boron from Boron, California}. AlBN switches like AlScN but needs no scandium (imported), so every element in the stack (Al, B, N, Si, Mo) is mined and refined in the U.S.
why: Scarce-resource intensity and U.S. manufacturability: nonvolatile and refresh-free with a fully domestic element list; the architecture covers the endurance gap.

title: Liquid-nitrogen planar DRAM: helium-free cold shrinks the capacitor tenfold
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a planar 0.5 fF ZrO2 MIM with no pillar | access: Si FET at 77 K | sense: low-noise cryogenic SA | integration: memory sleds immersed in LN2 from U.S. air-separation plants | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: relaxed-pitch patterning with a U.S. multibeam e-beam writer}. At 77 K subthreshold and junction leakage drop by more than 1e6, so retention reaches minutes even with a tiny planar capacitor, and nitrogen cooling avoids the helium chokepoint entirely.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no high-AR capacitor, essentially no refresh, no EUV; LN2 is cheap and made domestically.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-silicon-oxide gain cell from domestic zinc
idea: Box = {medium: charge on the gate node of a read transistor | access: amorphous Zn-Si-O write TFT (wide gap, ultralow off-current) | sense: gain-cell read current | integration: 4-8 monolithic BEOL tiers | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: ALD with zinc from Alaska + U.S. silane}. Si suppresses oxygen vacancies in ZnO the way Ga does in IGZO, aiming for aA-level off-current without indium (mostly imported) or gallium (~98% Chinese).
why: Scarce resources and U.S. manufacturability: removes In and Ga from oxide-semiconductor DRAM while keeping long retention and 3D tiers.

title: Parametron revived: AlN nanoresonator phase bits made in U.S. filter fabs
idea: Box = {medium: 0 or pi oscillation phase of a parametrically pumped 2-5 GHz AlN nanoresonator | access: frequency-multiplexed pump rows, no transistor | sense: phase-sensitive mixer per column | integration: resonator arrays released over CMOS | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: the AlN BAW/FBAR filter lines already running in Colorado and Texas}. Goto's 1954 parametron stored bits as subharmonic phase; at Q~1e4 and aJ stored energy the pump dissipates ~0.1 pW per bit, and a write injects a seed tone during pump ramp-up.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no leakage and no capacitor, static energy comparable to DRAM refresh, built with domestic MEMS capacity instead of DRAM fabs.

title: VO2 bistable inside its thermal hysteresis, erased by piezo-AlN strain
idea: Box = {medium: metallic vs insulating phase of VO2 held inside its hysteresis loop at a 65 C die temperature | access: Si FET | sense: ~100x resistance ratio | integration: VO2 on a piezoelectric AlN underlayer | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputtered VO2 from Utah vanadium}. A Joule pulse writes the metallic phase, and a strain pulse from the AlN underlayer shifts the transition temperature above the die temperature so the cell snaps back to insulating; at idle both phases are stable with no power.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no refresh, an all-domestic V/Al/N/Si stack, and it uses the heat DRAM dies already run at.

title: Dynamic copper-filament crosspoint memory refreshed like DRAM
idea: Box = {medium: volatile nanoscale Cu filament in SiO2 that dissolves over ~1 s | access: none (self-rectifying stack) | sense: filament on/off current ~1e3 | integration: 4F2 crosspoint stacked 8 layers | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputtered Arizona copper + PECVD SiO2}. Filaments are kept deliberately thin so they relax on their own, which allows low compliance current and longer endurance, and a 1 s refresh rewrites the ones.
why: Density (4F2 x 8 layers) and capital: a crosspoint with no access transistor, built from only Cu, Si and O.

title: All-silicon vertical gated thyristor: bistable bit from boron, phosphorus, silicon
idea: Box = {medium: regenerative pnpn latch state | access: the thyristor's own gate | sense: on/off current ~1e5 | integration: vertical 4F2 pillars | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: in-situ doped epitaxy with California boron and U.S. phosphate phosphorus, NiSi contacts from Michigan nickel}. The cell contains only Si, B, P, O, N and Ni, so it needs no capacitor dielectric and no exotic metal.
why: U.S. manufacturability and scarce resources: a 4F2 cell that needs little refresh, with the shortest supply chain possible.

title: Grown carbon-nanotube forest capacitors replacing etched pillars
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD dielectric coating a 30 nm vertically aligned CNT bundle | access: vertical Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: DSA-patterned Fe catalyst dots (Minnesota iron) + CVD growth from U.S. natural-gas methane}. Each cell's electrode grows 3 um tall from its catalyst dot instead of being etched, giving surface area beyond AR 100:1 without any high-AR plasma etch.
why: Fact 1 and capital (Fact 4): growth replaces the most expensive etch module, using domestic carbon and iron.

title: Rare-earth-free Fe16N2 nanomagnet SOT cell from Minnesota iron nitride
idea: Box = {medium: high-anisotropy alpha''-Fe16N2 free layer | access: Si FET | sense: TMR with MgO from Michigan brine | integration: BEOL 3-terminal SOT cell | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputter + low-temperature nitridation from the U.S. Fe16N2 magnet industry}. Fe16N2's high magnetization and anisotropy keep a bit stable at ~15 nm without Pt, Co or rare earths, and spin-orbit-torque writes keep current out of the tunnel barrier for DRAM-class endurance.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: removes Co, Pt, Ir, Ru and rare earths; nonvolatile and refresh-free.

title: Scanner-free cell arrays: laser interference lithography plus e-beam periphery
idea: Box = {medium: charge on pillar capacitors | access: vertical FET | sense: standard SA | integration: periodic array patterned separately from the periphery | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: 4-beam 193 nm interference exposure from U.S. lasers gives a defect-free ~68 nm pitch dot lattice, pitch-split 2-4x by ALD spacers, while a U.S. multibeam writer exposes only the irregular periphery}. Cell arrays are perfectly periodic, so they need interference, not imaging, which removes imported scanners and masks.
why: Fact 4 and the EUV chokepoint: the cell array needs no photomask or scanner, cutting lithography capex by ~10x.

title: Nano-DMD torsion latch: Texas micromirror physics shrunk to memory bits
idea: Box = {medium: landed-left or landed-right state of a 100 nm torsion-hinge paddle | access: row/column electrostatic half-select | sense: capacitive tilt sensing | integration: MEMS over CMOS as in DLP | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: the Dallas DLP flow (Al hinges, SAM anti-stiction, spring tips)}. A small hold bias keeps the paddle latched on its landing tip; DLP mirrors already pass 1e12 landings with stiction controlled, and shrinking ~50x raises the resonance to GHz for ns switching.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no charge leakage and no destructive read; an existing domestic MEMS base becomes memory capacity.

title: Element passport: incentives only for cells built from domestic elements
idea: Box constraint as policy: CHIPS and DPA Title III funds and a federal purchasing preference go only to storage-element stacks whose every element (e.g., Si, Al, B, N, O, Hf, Zr, Mo, Cu, Zn, Fe, Ti, Pt/Pd, V, Te) has U.S. primary production, with matched loans for domestic high-purity Hf/Zr/Mo ALD-precursor plants. Each cell design files a bill of elements traced to a U.S. mine or refinery.
why: Scarce-resource intensity and U.S. manufacturability: steers R&D toward chokepoint-free stacks before fabs lock in W, Ru, Sc or Ga.

title: Elemental-tellurium dynamic phase-change cell that self-erases
idea: Box = {medium: metastable amorphous vs crystalline elemental Te in a 10 nm confined pore | access: Si FET | sense: ~1e3 resistance ratio | integration: BEOL with Mo heater | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: evaporated Te recovered at Utah copper refineries}. Confined amorphous Te recrystallizes on its own in ~seconds at 85 C, so the cell is deliberately dynamic: a ~10 ns quench writes a one, decay plus refresh handles the rest, and no Ge or Sb is needed.
why: Scarce resources and U.S. manufacturability: a one-element storage medium from a domestic byproduct, with retention set by crystallization kinetics rather than transistor leakage.

title: Chain-cell PZT FeRAM on a Texas line with domestic electrodes
idea: Box = {medium: PZT polarization | access: chain architecture, each FeCap in parallel with its transistor and cells linked in series (4F2-class) | sense: destructive charge read with in-chain restore | integration: 3D trench FeCaps | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: Dallas-style PZT module using Missouri lead, Oregon zirconium, and LaNiO3 conductive-oxide electrodes from California lanthanum and Michigan nickel}. Conductive-oxide electrodes suppress PZT fatigue toward 1e12-1e14 cycles, and a small SRAM cache absorbs hot writes.
why: U.S. manufacturability: scales a production-proven domestic ferroelectric line from niche to bulk memory; refresh-free, with no Ir or Ru.

title: Storage layer on the backside power network of U.S. logic
idea: Box = {medium: charge on BEOL MIM capacitors | access: low-temperature Zn-based oxide TFTs | sense: SAs in the front-side logic | integration: memory tier built on the wafer backside after backside-power processing, plate tied to the backside power mesh | substrate: U.S.-made leading-edge logic wafers (Arizona/Oregon) | fab: <400 C backside ALD}. The thinned backside otherwise carries only power rails; a 1T1C tier there puts several MB per mm2 directly under the compute with sub-micron vertical paths.
why: Fact 5 data-movement energy (~10x below HBM) and U.S. manufacturability: memory capacity from domestic leading-edge logic fabs that already exist.

title: National capacitor-module line where startups drop in new storage elements
idea: Box as infrastructure: a government-anchored 300 mm U.S. line runs standard domestic periphery and access-transistor wafers to the capacitor level, then lets startups insert their own storage-element module (AAO, CNT, rutile TiO2, AlBN and others) and finishes BEOL. Teams pay per wafer and keep their IP.
why: Capital intensity (Fact 4): proving a new storage element costs ~$50M instead of a $15B fab and shortens lab-to-1-Gb proof from ~8 years to ~3.

title: Pinned-photodiode-style buried well storing 200 electrons, image-sensor readout
idea: Box = {medium: ~200 electrons in a buried n-well pinned by a p+ surface layer | access: transfer gate | sense: high-conversion-gain floating diffusion (~150 uV per electron) shared by 4 cells | integration: 4-shared cell like a CMOS image-sensor pixel | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: image-sensor implant flow on U.S. lines (e.g., Idaho)}. Surface pinning suppresses interface generation so dark current is a few electrons per second, and low-noise image-sensor readout resolves 200 electrons where DRAM stores ~15,000, so the well itself is the capacitor.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no stacked capacitor and refresh intervals of seconds, using domestic image-sensor process know-how.

title: Gated-diode amplifying storage node that boosts its own signal
idea: Box = {medium: charge in a Si gated-diode (MOS varactor) node | access: one Si FET | sense: on read the gate is pulsed so the varactor drops from inversion to depletion capacitance (~5x lower), raising node voltage ~5x before charge sharing | integration: planar 2T-class cell | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: standard domestic CMOS with no high-k capacitor}. The storage element amplifies itself (Q fixed, C collapses), so the cell needs only ~1 fF and no pillar.
why: Fact 1 and capital: removes the high-AR capacitor and its dielectric, so the cell can be built on existing domestic logic lines.

title: Redox-molecule monolayer storage node with built-in multi-level voltages
idea: Box = {medium: electrons held in surface-tethered porphyrin/ferrocene molecules with discrete oxidation potentials | access: Si FET | sense: charge read against molecule-defined levels (2 bits per cell) | integration: monolayer grafted inside a short pillar | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: U.S.-synthesized molecules attached from solution, following the North Carolina molecular-memory lineage}. Each oxidation state releases charge at a potential fixed by chemistry, so the multi-level references calibrate themselves, and retention comes from slow electron-transfer kinetics rather than transistor leakage.
why: Density (2 bits per cell) and Fact 3: chemistry sets the levels, avoiding ECC-heavy MLC sensing, using domestic organic chemistry.
